newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel suspends Hamas extradition from U.S. -radio.
newsitem.headline: Israel suspends Hamas extradition from U.S. -radio.

text.p: Israel will suspend its request for the United States to extradite an Islamic Hamas political leader, Israel Radio said on Thursday.
It said Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu took the decision on Mousa Mohammed Abu Marzook based on consultation with legal and security officials in Israel.
The radio quoted a statement from Netanyahu's office.

Israeli and U.S. officials want to avoid extraditing Abu Marzook to Israel in the middle of a crisis in U.S.-sponsored Middle East peacemaking. Abu Marzook gave up his fight against extradition in January.
In 1995 Israel announced it had formally asked the United States to hand over Abu Marzook, alleging he was responsible as the head of Hamas's political arm for attacks that killed scores of Israelis.

Israel did not contend that Abu Marzook personally committed any of the violent acts, but charged he was criminally liable because of his high-level role in allegedly directing, controlling and financially supporting Hamas's activities. Abu Marzook has denied involvement in any violence.
